summary:
Source 1 — VMSG_RAG_Content_Factory.pdf (4 pages, "VMSG — RAG Content Factory, System Design"): describes a batch hybrid GraphRAG system (vector + knowledge graph) that is strictly generation-side with ZERO runtime consumers — scope was locked 2026-07-17 as "a nightly run plus an hourly top-up, and the chatbot does not consume RAG." The system works through six math books and a topic map on a schedule, generates practice questions with AI, verifies them, and stores them so students only ever see pre-checked content. It is organized as four lanes shown on an Excalidraw board (interactive URL included): Lane 1 Ingestion (blue) — runs only when a new book is added; pipeline stations are 0) chunker (cuts books into teaching-unit chunks — one explanation/worked example/problem per chunk, tagged with type, book, page number, and a content_hash fingerprint for dedup), 1) digitizer (PDF → plain text/markdown, needed because LangExtract can't read PDFs), 2) context+embedding (1,536-dim vector via OpenAI text-embedding-3-small stored in Postgres pgvector, nearest-neighbor lookup, NFKC Unicode normalization, checkpoint file for resumable runs), 3) LangExtract (the only AI step in ingestion — extracts skills/techniques/traps/examples with a hard rule that every fact must point to exact supporting source characters or be discarded; being piloted on a single Tirthaji chapter), 4) SymPy math audit (recomputes every answer, 5-second ceiling per check, circuit breaker after 10 consecutive timeouts), 5) dual-DB ingest via MERGE (idempotent) writing text+vectors to Postgres and entities+relationships to Neo4j. Lane 2 Storage: PostgreSQL+pgvector "the Ledger" (4,943 existing chunks + vectors, generated problems with fingerprint dedup, per-problem trust score, audit log of every AI call, replenishment history, reference-library pages); Neo4j "the GPS" topic map (467 Skills, 807 Problems, 791 SolveAlongs, 590 Explainers, 908 Traps, 16 Sutras, 6 Books; relationships MANIFESTS_AS, FRONTIER_OF, NEXT_TOPIC, REQUIRES, PREREQUISITE_OF, plus SolveAlongs-teach-Skills / Explainers-explain-Skills pointing back to Books, and Problems/SolveAlongs → Traps); Redis "the warm tray" (overnight-generated questions held 24h for instant app reads, recently-seen fingerprint list, AI-spend counters); and a deliberately thin 3-wire integration surface (two Celery task-name stubs already scheduled by the main repo, the Postgres tables, the Redis tray). The most important rule is game-loop isolation: no AI/retrieval while a student practises. Lane 3 Nightly Batch Factory at 00:00 UTC (Celery beat trigger, hard token budget): pool composer finds low subtopics using the map + already-seen/already-mastered lists; generation runs T1 (1,505 ready-made templates, no AI) and T2 (pattern + seeded-random numbers, 100 per pattern, arithmetic-rechecked); everything passes the 7-stage auditor (fields present → LaTeX renders → SymPy math check → domain rules e.g. valid base → declared traps make sense → dedup → 2-of-3 AI judges, the only AI use in this lane); then a trust ladder QUARANTINED → SANDBOX (max 50 exposures, never counts toward mastery/mock exams) → TRUSTED → LIVE, with pattern freeze after 3 quarantined questions from one pattern; write-out saves to Postgres, loads Redis, and files a run report (tokens spent, pass rate, pool depth). Lane 4 Hourly Replenishment: if a subtopic's unused pool drops below 50, make 100 more via an escalation ladder T1 resample (no AI, wider number variation, stricter dedup) → T2 escalate to next difficulty (no AI) → T3 bridge from a prerequisite/sibling subtopic max one hop away (no AI) → T4 LLM regenerate (rare safety valve: AI writes template variants grounded in map context + top-5 book chunks, then SymPy + jury) → T5 convert explainer examples into questions by hiding steps/shuffling numbers (no AI, fires an alert if reached); total failure degrades gracefully (widen topic, review mode, mastery summary, end session). All hourly output loops back through the 7-stage auditor — no side door into the pool. Retrieval design: two-step (topic-filter via graph first, then cosine-similarity ranking, keep top 5, discard below 0.70; pg_trgm keyword fallback for formulas), used in exactly three places, all inside the factory. Known cleanup debts flagged: the existing 4,943 chunks have messy type labels; the ontology registry's embeddings are all zeros (never computed) and must be regenerated; the old schema file says :Technique nodes but the live DB uses :Skill — code against :Skill.

Source 2 — pipeline-untitled.pdf (12 pages, "Graph Closure Extraction Strategies: Deep Architecture Guide"): despite the filename this is NOT the OCR/extraction pipeline — it is an architecture guide for precomputing transitive prerequisite closures ("what must a student know before X?") from the Neo4j AuraDB Free-tier prerequisite graph (:Technique nodes, [:PREREQUISITE_OF] edges — note the :Technique/:Skill naming discrepancy flagged in source 1). The naive [:PREREQUISITE_OF*1..5] Cypher causes Cartesian explosion and OOM/timeouts on AuraDB Free's JVM heap. Four strategies: A) APOC BFS via apoc.path.spanningTree (relationshipFilter "PREREQUISITE_OF>", minLevel 1, maxLevel 5, limit 1000 per start node; cycle-free, bounded memory; built into AuraDB; ~2-5s per 1,000 start nodes; fails past ~15,000 nodes with avg degree ~8) — the immediate Week-2 fix, a query swap in the Neo4jDesignTimeCompiler Python script; B) Topic-partitioned batching — loop over taxonomy.yaml topics (examples: VedicMath, NumberTheory, Algebra, Geometry), query one subgraph at a time, per-topic Postgres commits via psycopg2 execute_values into prerequisite_closure, parallelizable with ThreadPoolExecutor; requires a topic property on nodes (which they should have from taxonomy.yaml ingestion); use when Strategy A times out; C) Postgres Recursive CTE — Neo4j exports only depth-1 edges (~100ms, tiny payload) into stg_prerequisites (ancestor_hash/descendant_hash/depth, PK on the hash pair), then WITH RECURSIVE computes depths 2-5 on disk with MIN(depth) keeping shortest paths; "Ledger vs GPS" principle; for Phase 3 (10K+ nodes / cross-category routing) on the project's $12 Droplet Postgres; D) Incremental delta sync — updated_at timestamps on nodes, query only changed nodes since last_sync (from a sync_manifest table), recompute only affected subtrees via spanningTree, upsert; ~20x speedup since 1-5% of nodes change daily; Phase 4 only, hardest (partial-invalidation logic). Includes a benchmarking protocol: prerequisite_closure_test shadow table plus a sync_manifest table (source, target_table, status dry_run/production, started_at, completed_at, record_count, execution_time_ms, memory_peak_mb, error_message) and a benchmark_closure_strategies.py loop; decision thresholds (<70% peak JVM heap via the AuraDB dashboard, <30s total execution, <5MB per batch payload, <5s Postgres ingestion); a decision matrix; and a phased rollout: Phase 1 Launch Weeks 1-15 Strategy A, Phase 2 Scale Weeks 16-21 A→B, Phase 3 Cross-Subject Months 4-6 C, Phase 4 Mature Month 7+ D.

Gaps relative to the briefing questions: NEITHER PDF names an OCR engine (the ingestion "digitizer" station converts PDF→text/markdown but no tool is specified), neither mentions an "os-taxonomy" repo by that name (only taxonomy.yaml and "the main repo"), neither names the generation/judge LLM models, and there are no dashboards beyond the nightly run report and the AuraDB monitoring dashboard. The books are described only as "the six math books" — no CAT/GRE/Nishit K Sinha titles appear in these two PDFs. Other files in the same directory likely carry those details: VMSG_TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md, VMSG_CONTENT_READINESS.md, VMSG_CLIENT_BRIEF.md, VMSG_PROGRESS_REPORT.pdf, gre_preview.html, preview-1.html, preview-2.html, system-design.excalidraw (all under /Users/harshahirrao/Speed gym/docs/reference/).
key_facts: Scope locked 2026-07-17: RAG is batch/generation-side only — nightly run at 00:00 UTC + hourly top-up; chatbot does NOT consume RAG; zero runtime consumers
Hard rule: game-loop isolation — no AI, no retrieval, fully offline while a student is practising
Hybrid GraphRAG = vector side (what the six books say) + graph side (how topics relate)

Corpus: 4,943 existing chunks from six math books (PDFs); chunks are teaching-unit sized (one explanation/worked example/problem each) with book + page number + content_hash fingerprint for dedup; existing chunks have messy type labels needing cleanup

Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, 1,536 dimensions, stored in Postgres via pgvector (no separate vector DB); embedded once at ingest; checkpoint file makes runs resumable; ontology registry embeddings are all zeros (never computed) and must be regenerated
Retrieval: 2-step — graph topic filter first, then cosine similarity, top-5 kept, threshold 0.70 cutoff; pg_trgm keyword fallback for formulas; used in exactly 3 places, all inside the factory

Ingestion Lane stations: 0 chunker → 1 digitizer (PDF→text/markdown; LangExtract cannot read PDFs) → 2 context+embedding (1,536-dim vector, nearest-neighbor lookup, NFKC normalization) → 3 LangExtract (extracts skills/techniques/traps/examples; every fact must cite exact source characters or is discarded — anti-hallucination guard; piloted on a single Tirthaji chapter first) → 4 SymPy math audit (5s ceiling per check; circuit breaker trips after 10 consecutive timeouts) → 5 dual-DB ingest with MERGE (idempotent re-runs) into Postgres + Neo4j
Postgres 'Ledger' holds: chunks+vectors, generated problems (fingerprint dedup), per-problem trust score, audit log of every AI call, replenishment history, reference-library pages
Neo4j 'GPS' node counts: 467 Skills, 807 Problems, 791 SolveAlongs (guided walkthroughs), 590 Explainers (lesson cards), 908 Traps (common mistakes), 16 Sutras (Vedic formulas), 6 Books

Neo4j relationships: Sutra-MANIFESTS_AS->Skill; Skill-FRONTIER_OF/NEXT_TOPIC/REQUIRES->Skill (learning order); Skill-PREREQUISITE_OF->Problem; SolveAlongs teach Skills, Explainers explain Skills, both point back to source Book; Problems and SolveAlongs point to Traps
Schema discrepancy: old schema file says :Technique nodes, live DB uses :Skill — always code against :Skill (the closure-strategies PDF still uses :Technique throughout)
Redis 'warm tray': overnight questions held 24h for instant app reads; also recently-seen fingerprint list and AI-spend counters
Integration surface is deliberately 3 wires: two Celery task names already scheduled by the main repo (currently empty stubs to fill in), the Postgres tables, the Redis tray

Nightly factory: Celery beat trigger at 00:00 UTC with hard token budget; pool composer checks map + already-seen + already-mastered lists; generation T1 = 1,505 ready-made templates (no AI), T2 = seeded-random pattern instantiation, 100 per pattern, arithmetic-rechecked immediately

7-stage auditor (every question, both lanes, no side door): 1 all fields present, 2 LaTeX renders, 3 SymPy math check, 4 domain rules (e.g. chosen base valid), 5 declared traps make sense, 6 not a duplicate, 7 2-of-3 AI judges sign off (only AI in nightly lane)
Trust ladder: QUARANTINED → SANDBOX (max 50 exposures; never counts toward mastery scores or mock exams) → TRUSTED → LIVE; 3 quarantined questions from one pattern freezes the whole pattern
Nightly run report: tokens spent, pass rate, pool depth

Hourly replenishment: trigger when a subtopic's unused pool < 50, generate 100 more; escalation ladder T1 resample (no AI) → T2 next-difficulty escalate (no AI) → T3 bridge from prerequisite/sibling max 1 hop (no AI) → T4 LLM regenerate (grounded in map context + top-5 book chunks, then SymPy + jury) → T5 convert explainer examples to questions (no AI; fires alert if reached); full failure degrades gracefully (widen topic, review mode, mastery summary, polite session end)

Excalidraw system-design board URL: https://excalidraw.com/#json=tHfWlVQu3MQjAviTWGZ4y,nakbyPaaseSsjDy8UUYM5w (local copy: /Users/harshahirrao/Speed gym/docs/reference/system-design.excalidraw); four lanes colored ingestion blue, storage centre, nightly orange, hourly purple

pipeline-untitled.pdf is a graph-closure guide, not OCR: precomputing transitive prerequisite closure from Neo4j AuraDB Free (:Technique/[:PREREQUISITE_OF]); naive *1..5 traversal causes Cartesian explosion / OutOfMemoryError on Free-tier JVM heap

Strategy A (Weeks 1-15): apoc.path.spanningTree BFS, relationshipFilter 'PREREQUISITE_OF>', maxLevel 5, limit 1000/start node; APOC built into AuraDB; ~2-5s per 1,000 start nodes; fails past ~15K nodes at avg degree ~8; implemented as a Cypher swap in the Neo4jDesignTimeCompiler Python script

Strategy B (Weeks 16-21, on timeouts): loop over taxonomy.yaml topics (VedicMath, NumberTheory, Algebra, Geometry), per-topic subgraph queries, psycopg2 execute_values batch insert into prerequisite_closure, per-topic commits, ThreadPoolExecutor-parallelizable; needs topic property on nodes from taxonomy.yaml ingestion

Strategy C (Months 4-6, 10K+ nodes): Neo4j exports depth-1 edges only (~100ms) into stg_prerequisites(ancestor_hash, descendant_hash, depth; PK on hash pair); Postgres WITH RECURSIVE computes depth 2-5 on disk, MIN(depth) keeps shortest path; runs on the project's $12 Droplet Postgres

Strategy D (Month 7+): incremental delta sync — updated_at on nodes, query nodes changed since last sync (timestamp from sync_manifest), recompute only affected subtrees, upsert; ~20x speedup (1-5% of nodes change daily); hardest part is partial invalidation; only after graph is stable and daily syncs exceed 10 min

Benchmark protocol: prerequisite_closure_test shadow table + sync_manifest table (source, target_table, status 'dry_run'/'production', started_at, completed_at, record_count, execution_time_ms, memory_peak_mb, error_message) + benchmark_closure_strategies.py; thresholds: <70% peak JVM heap (AuraDB dashboard), <30s total execution, <5MB per batch network payload, <5s Postgres ingestion
Hybrid B+C recommended when some topics are dense and some sparse

NOT in these PDFs: no OCR engine named (digitizer station tool unspecified), no 'os-taxonomy' repo mention (only taxonomy.yaml + 'the main repo'), no generation/judge LLM model names, no dashboards beyond nightly run report and AuraDB monitoring, no CAT/GRE/Nishit K Sinha book titles (books called only 'the six math books')

decisions_and_status: Decision (locked 2026-07-17): RAG is generation-side only — nightly batch at 00:00 UTC + hourly replenishment; no runtime RAG consumers; chatbot excluded from RAG per the owner's call
Decision: game-loop isolation — no AI or retrieval during student practice sessions
Decision: dual store never collapsed into one — Postgres+pgvector for text/vectors/records, Neo4j for topic graph, Redis for the 24h serving tray; no separate vector database
Decision: all generated questions pass the 7-stage auditor and climb the QUARANTINED→SANDBOX→TRUSTED→LIVE trust ladder; no side door into the pool; pattern freeze after 3 quarantines
Decision: minimize AI usage — nightly generation is template-based (T1/T2, no AI except 2-of-3 judge stage); hourly ladder reaches AI only at T4; hard token budget per nightly run

Decision (architect's phased plan for closure extraction): Phase 1 Weeks 1-15 Strategy A (APOC BFS), Phase 2 Weeks 16-21 add Strategy B (topic-partitioned) on timeouts, Phase 3 Months 4-6 Strategy C (Postgres recursive CTE), Phase 4 Month 7+ Strategy D (incremental delta sync); benchmark strategies via shadow table + sync_manifest before switching

Status at time of writing: 4,943 chunks ingested from a prior ingestion run (shelves stocked from day one); 1,505 T1 templates exist; Neo4j populated (467 Skills / 807 Problems / 791 SolveAlongs / 590 Explainers / 908 Traps / 16 Sutras / 6 Books)

Status/debt: chunk type labels messy (cleanup is part of the build); ontology-registry embeddings all zero, to be regenerated; old schema file uses :Technique while live DB uses :Skill; LangExtract only at pilot stage (one Tirthaji chapter); the two Celery tasks scheduled by the main repo are empty stubs to be filled in

Task status: both PDFs read in full (4 + 12 pages); pipeline-untitled.pdf turned out to be the graph-closure architecture guide, not an OCR pipeline doc — OCR/book-extraction specifics must come from other sources in /Users/harshahirrao/Speed gym/docs/reference/

workstream_notes.backend: Backend touchpoints are deliberately minimal: two Celery tasks (nightly 00:00 UTC beat + hourly replenishment) that the main repo already schedules as empty stubs, the Postgres tables the factory writes, and the Redis tray the app reads (questions cached 24h). Enforce game-loop isolation — the practice loop must never call AI or retrieval. The prerequisite_closure table in Postgres (fed from Neo4j via the Neo4jDesignTimeCompiler script, Strategy A APOC BFS first, later B/C/D per the phased plan) is what the app should query for 'what must the student know before X' — never traverse Neo4j at runtime. Infrastructure named: $12 DigitalOcean Droplet running Postgres (with pgvector + pg_trgm), Neo4j AuraDB Free tier, Redis, Celery. Supporting tables to build: prerequisite_closure, stg_prerequisites, sync_manifest (schema given in full), prerequisite_closure_test.
workstream_notes.data_extraction: The ingestion pipeline (Lane 1, runs only when adding a book) is: station 0 chunker (teaching-unit chunks — one explanation/worked example/problem each; type tag, book, page, content_hash) → 1 digitizer (PDF→text/markdown; tool NOT specified in these PDFs; required because LangExtract cannot read PDFs) → 2 embedding+context (text-embedding-3-small 1,536-dim into pgvector, NFKC normalization, nearest-neighbor context, resumable via checkpoint file) → 3 LangExtract structured-fact extraction (skills/techniques/traps/examples; character-level source grounding mandatory, ungrounded facts discarded; pilot = one Tirthaji chapter) → 4 SymPy answer recomputation (5s/check, circuit breaker at 10 consecutive timeouts) → 5 idempotent MERGE dual-write to Postgres + Neo4j. Existing corpus: 4,943 chunks with messy type labels to clean; ontology-registry embeddings are zeros and need regeneration. Note the mismatch with the orchestrator's framing: these PDFs never mention OCR engines, CAT/GRE books, or Nishit K Sinha — only 'the six math books' and Tirthaji; the OCR specifics live elsewhere.
workstream_notes.rag: The RAG design is batch hybrid GraphRAG with zero runtime consumers (locked 2026-07-17; chatbot excluded). Retrieval = graph topic filter → cosine top-5 with 0.70 floor → pg_trgm keyword fallback for formulas, used in exactly 3 factory-internal spots. Generation economics: T1 templates (1,505) and T2 seeded-random instantiation cover the nightly run with AI only at the 2-of-3 judge stage; hourly ladder T1-T3 and T5 are AI-free, T4 (LLM regenerate grounded in graph context + top-5 chunks) is the sole AI generation path and T5 fires an operator alert. Quality gates: 7-stage auditor (fields, LaTeX render, SymPy, domain rules, trap sanity, dedup, 2-of-3 AI judges) + trust ladder QUARANTINED→SANDBOX(≤50 exposures, excluded from mastery/mocks)→TRUSTED→LIVE + pattern freeze at 3 quarantines + hard nightly token budget + audit log of every AI call + nightly run report (tokens, pass rate, pool depth). Graph schema and counts (467 Skills etc., relationships MANIFESTS_AS/FRONTIER_OF/NEXT_TOPIC/REQUIRES/PREREQUISITE_OF) are the content-factory's topic map; code against :Skill, not the stale :Technique in the schema file and in the closure-strategies doc.
